rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sekīnet means tranquility, assurance, steadfastness, and composure: the soul's calm after its agitation and anxiety cease.
rows.anchor: “Sekînet” sükûn ve itmi’nan, sebat ve temkin mânasına masdardır

rows.speaker: Râgıb
rows.claim: God's sending down a blessing means granting it, either by sending the thing itself, as with the Qur'an, or by sending its means and guiding the servant, as with iron.
rows.anchor: Râgıb der ki: “Allah teâlâ’nın kuluna nimetini inzâli i‘tâsı demektir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here, 'settling' may mean making believers' hearts a dwelling and resting place for sekīnet.
rows.anchor: burada kondurmak kalblerini sekînete menzil ve makar yapmak mânasına da olur

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Ali
rows.claim: A report from Ali describes sekīnet as an angel dwelling in a believer's heart and reassuring it.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali’den bir rivayette de denilmiştir ki “sekînet mü’minin kalbine sâkin olup onu temin eyleyen bir melektir

rows.speaker: Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye
rows.claim: Sekīnet begins with contemplating God's command comprehensively from every aspect; without that, true tranquility is impossible.
rows.anchor: Sekînetin başlangıcı, emri her vechile ihâta tarîkiyle mütalaadır. Böyle olmayınca sekînet sahih olmaz

rows.speaker: Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye
rows.claim: Abraham's request to see how God revives the dead arose because differing possibilities unsettled him; witnessing the manner ended his agitation.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ ona keyfiyeti müşahede ettirince o muhtelif vücûhtan gelen cezbelerle ıztırabdan sükûna eriverdi

rows.speaker: Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye
rows.claim: For a desired or feared matter, tranquility begins when its attainment is realized or despair of attaining it settles the question.
rows.anchor: yahut tahsîlinden yeis o matlab hakkında sekînetin başı olduğu gibi

rows.speaker: Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye
rows.claim: When a believer perfects and strengthens faith's conditions, God's manifestation in the heart is called 'taste.'
rows.anchor: o tecellîye ‘zevk’ tesmiye edilir

rows.speaker: Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye
rows.claim: Sekīnet is a threshold and ladder toward the realization of the unseen matter believed in, making it familiar like confidence in ordinary causes.
rows.anchor: o sekînet onun için iman vâki‘olacak gāib emrin husûlüne bir kapı ve bir merdiven olsun

rows.speaker: Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye
rows.claim: Such certainty comes through direct experience, not from the unseen; a person with a day's food is calm because he sees it in his possession.
rows.anchor: Bu ise asla gaybdan olmaz; belki zevkten, yani mu‘âyeneden olur

rows.speaker: Fütûhât-ı Mekkiyye
rows.claim: A believer has sekīnet when faith's rule is realized as directly as the food example; if direct awareness contends with faith's ruling, sekīnet is absent.
rows.anchor: münâza‘a ediyorsa onda sekînet hâsıl olmamıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A heart-quality can also receive an external sign in chosen servants; the sign takes the quality's name, as with the form called sekīnet placed in Israel's Ark and read as a sign of victory.
rows.anchor: Benî İsrâil’in Tabut’unda böyle bir sekîne konulmuştu ki o bir şekil bir suret idi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For this community, sekīnet's proper locus is the heart, and its inner presence is its own evidence without an external sign.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ bu ümmet için sekînetin husûlüne kendilerinin hâricinden bir alâmet yapmamıştır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sekīnet is what makes the soul rest in a promise or attained aim; its name shares the root of stillness and evokes a knife cutting away contrary impulses.
rows.anchor: Buna ‘sekîne’ yahut ‘sekînet’ denilmesi şunun içindir ki, bu hâsıl olunca nefsin diğer cihete olan esintilerini keser atar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although stillness is the opposite of movement, sekīnet fixes the soul on what reassures it, even if that object is itself moving; it comes through contemplation or witnessing.
rows.anchor: Sekînet ise nefsin mutmain olduğu şey üzerine sübut verir ki velevse hareket olsun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sekīnet descends on believers and moves them from their level of faith to the station of direct witnessing.
rows.anchor: mü’minlerin üzerine iner ve inmesiyle onları bulundukları iman mertebesinden mu‘âyene makamına nakleder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Even if simple foundational faith neither increases nor decreases, its completeness increases as its supporting confirmations grow.
rows.anchor: Basit olan asl-ı imanda ziyade ve noksan olmasa bile müeyyidâtı arttıkça imanın kemâlinin de artacağında şüphe yoktur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: As faith's causes and objects multiply, monotheistic faith grows like a tree, expanding its branches until it bears the desired fruits.
rows.anchor: bir ağaç gibi fürû‘ve şu‘abâtını artıra artıra neşv ü nemâ bularak nihâyet matlub olan meyvelerini verir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Increase or decrease in foundational faith means strength or weakness, since assent is not a matter of quantity.
rows.anchor: ziyade ve noksan, şiddet ve za‘f ile tefsir olunur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's ownership of heaven's and earth's armies signals surrendering all things to Him through the comprehensive vision that begins sekīnet.
rows.anchor: Sekînetin mebde’i olan ihâtalı görgü ile bütün eşyâyı Allah teâlâ’ya teslîme işarettir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: All forces above and below belong to God, who gives victory as He wills; sekīnet in believers' hearts is one of His armies, dispelling pagan agitation, increasing faith, and enabling success and great victories.
rows.anchor: mü’minlerin kalbine indirdiği sekînet de O’nun cünûdundan biridir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows everything and wisely determines and manages all affairs.
rows.anchor: her şeyi ve bütün umûru kemâl-i ilim ile bilir ve hikmet ile takdir ve tedbir eyler

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge and wisdom govern the armies of heaven and earth, sometimes setting them against one another and sometimes making peace between them.
rows.anchor: gâh birbirine taslit ederek ve gâh beynlerinde sulh yaptırarak tedbir ve idare eder

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some attach the purpose clause to forgiveness, God's support, or increased faith; following Zamakhshari and other investigators, the author prefers attaching it to the knowledge and wisdom implied by 'All-Knowing, Wise.'
rows.anchor: Zemahşerî gibi muhakkikīnin muhtârına göre عَلِيمًا حَكِيمًۭا’dan münfehim olan ilm ü hikmetin

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One wise result of managing the armies is sending sekīnet into believers' hearts, making them receptive to Hudaybiya's peace and preparing them for great conquests.
rows.anchor: Hudeybiye sulhuna ısındırarak büyük fütûhâta ihzar etmesidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does this so believers recognize His blessings, give thanks, merit reward, enter His gardens, and attain the greatest success.
rows.anchor: mü’minlere ondaki nimetlerini tanıtsın, şükrünü edâ etsinler, sevâba müstahik olsunlar da onları cennetlerine koysun

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will punish hypocrites and idolaters who dislike this outcome; hypocrites are named first because they harm Muslims more than idolaters do.
rows.anchor: Münafıkların Müslümanlara zararı müşriklerden daha çok olduğu için evvelâ onların ta‘zîbi söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those with evil thoughts about God assume He will not help His Messenger and believers, anticipate their harm and nonreturn to their families, and neither trust God nor seek His good and mercy.
rows.anchor: Allah Peygamberine ve mü’minlere yardım etmez sanırlar

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evil that the ill-wishers plot will circle back on them as a destructive whirlpool or storm.
rows.anchor: kötülük dairesi, yani fesad girdabı yahut kasırgası başlarına dönesiler

rows.speaker: müfessirler
rows.claim: The repeated reminder that heaven's and earth's armies belong to God points to His armies of both mercy and punishment; the second occurrence means the armies of punishment, with 'Mighty, Wise' stressing warning after the earlier glad tidings.
rows.anchor: Allah teâlâ’nın hem rahmet orduları hem de azab orduları bulunduğuna tenbihtir

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Commentators take the Messenger's being a witness to mean that he witnesses his community's deeds, in line with 2:143.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Burada müfessirîn وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًۭا [el-Bakara 2/143] medlûlünce ümmetin fiillerine şâhid demişlerdir

rows.speaker: Fahreddin Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says it is better to understand the Messenger as a witness to God's oneness, as in 3:18 and the command in 47:19.
rows.anchor: Fahreddin Râzî der ki: “Burada müfessirîn وَيَكُونَ ٱلرَّسُولُ عَلَيْكُمْ شَهِيدًۭا [el-Bakara 2/143] medlûlünce ümmetin fiillerine şâhid demişlerdir. Lâkin evlâ olan شَهِدَ ٱللَّهُ أَنَّهُۥ لَآ إِلَٰهَ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Messenger brings glad tidings to those who accept the testimony and act on it, and warning to those who do not accept it.
rows.anchor: o şehadeti kabul edip mûcebince amel edenlere müjdeci

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One grammatical reading makes the four commands follow respectively from the sending, witnessing, glad tidings, and warning: sending entails belief, witnessing entails supporting the religion, glad tidings entails honoring, and warning entails glorification and praise for protection from punishment.
rows.anchor: yani dinine nusret ile takviyeyi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second reading makes each of the four commands follow from each of the Messenger's four functions; on both readings all pronouns refer to God.
rows.anchor: Bunların dördü mecmû‘u evvelkilerin her birine terettüb eder ki bu da ikinci mânadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading refers the pronouns in supporting and honoring to the Messenger and the pronoun in glorifying to God; the Qur'anic stop sign at 'honor him' reflects this reading.
rows.anchor: وَتُعَزِّرُوهُ وَتُوَقِّرُوهُ zamirleri Resûl’e, وَتُسَبِّحُوهُ zamiri Allah’a râci‘olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pledging to the Messenger in his capacity as God's messenger is pledging to God, since obeying the Messenger is obeying the One who sent him; the author also points to 9:111.
rows.anchor: resûle resul olması haysiyetiyle itaat onu gönderene itaattir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse concerns the Pledge of Ridwan beneath the tree at Hudaybiya, when the companions pledged not to flee or to die; its wording has a general sense.
rows.anchor: Hudeybiye’de ağacın altında yapılan Bey‘at-ı Rıdvan hakkındadır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's hand above their hands portrays the pledge as a reciprocal contract, though its true benefit belongs to the pledgers because God's hand is above theirs.
rows.anchor: mübâya‘a bir alım satım gibi el ele vererek karşılıklı bir mukavele

rows.speaker: İbn Cerîr
rows.claim: Ibn Jarir gives two readings of God's hand above theirs: God's hand was above them as they pledged, since pledging to the Prophet was pledging to God; or God's power exceeds theirs.
rows.anchor: İbn Cerîr tefsirinde der ki: “Bunda iki vecih vardır

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the first reading, the Prophet is figuratively pictured as God's hand because he is God's messenger and instrument for carrying out His ordinances; God is not a bodily part of anything.
rows.anchor: kendisinden bir cüz olmak mânasına cârihadan münezzehtir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the second reading, 'hand' means power, might, or favor; either way, the pledge's direct benefit accrues to those who made it.
rows.anchor: cümle-i istînâfiye olarak “yed”, kuvvet ve kudret

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Breaking the pledge harms only the breaker; whoever fulfills the covenant with God will receive a great reward, namely Paradise and divine approval with delights beyond human perception.
rows.anchor: her kim cayarsa sırf kendi aleyhine olarak caymış olur

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After establishing the Messenger's mission and directing people to God's oneness through His mighty signs, the passage exposes the idols' worthlessness and the corruption of the Quraysh's beliefs.
rows.anchor: müşriklere mâbudlarının hakāreti, akidelerinin sekāmeti gösteriliyor

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is to Quraysh: after hearing this purely divine revelation and what their companion saw, they are challenged to say whether they saw al-Lat and al-Uzza.
rows.anchor: Hitab Kureyş’edir. Yani sırf vahy-i ilâhî olan

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat were idols the Arabs worshipped; they named people Abd al-Lat and Abd al-Uzza and swore by the idols.
rows.anchor: Lât, Uzzâ, Menât onların taptıkları putlardan idi

rows.speaker: Ebû Ubeyde ve bazıları
rows.claim: Some, including Abu Ubayda, say these were stone idols inside the Kaaba; the author instead judges they likely had separate shrines, since other idols such as Hubal were in the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: Ebû Ubeyde gibi bazıları bunların taştan putlar olup Kâbe’nin içinde bulunduklarını söylemişler ise de

rows.speaker: Mu‘cemü’l-büldan
rows.claim: Al-Lat's shrine was a white square stone temple built and staffed by Thaqif in Taif, revered by Quraysh and Arabs; it stood where Taif Mosque's left minaret is now.
rows.anchor: Lât Taif’te, Sakif beyaz murabba‘

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Thaqif entered Islam, the Prophet sent Abu Sufyan ibn Harb and al-Mughira ibn Shu'ba to demolish al-Lat's shrine.
rows.anchor: Sakif İslâm’a girdiğinde Resûlullah Ebû Süfyan b. Harb ile Muğîre b. Şu‘be’yi göndermiş

rows.speaker: Mu‘cemü’l-büldan
rows.claim: Al-Uzza was an idol beside a tree in Nakhla worshipped by Ghatafan, maintained by Banu Sayrima, and adopted by Zalim ibn Asad; its shrine was called Bess and a sound was heard inside.
rows.anchor: Uzzâ, Nahle’de bir ağaç yanında bir vesen idi, Gatafan ona ta‘abbüd ederdi

rows.speaker: Mu‘cemü’l-büldan
rows.claim: Quraysh and Arabs revered al-Uzza as Quraysh's greatest idol, visiting it and offering gifts and sacrifices; Quraysh also set aside a grove to imitate the Kaaba's sanctuary.
rows.anchor: Arab ve Kureyş ona tâzim ederlerdi ve Kureyş indinde esnâmın en büyüğü idi

rows.speaker: Dübeyye b. Harmî es-Selemî eş-Şeybânî
rows.claim: When Khalid came to cut al-Uzza's trees, its keeper Dübeyye urged the goddess to fight Khalid and threatened her with immediate humiliation if she failed.
rows.anchor: sâdini bulunan Dübeyye b. Harmî es-Selemî eş-Şeybânî

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At the Prophet's command, Khalid cut three trees at Batn Nakhla; at the third, a disheveled naked female devil appeared with the keeper behind her, and Khalid killed her and cut the tree.
rows.anchor: saçlarını dağıtmış, ellerini ensesine atmış dişlerini gösteriyordu

rows.speaker: Hazret-i Peygamber
rows.claim: After Khalid reported the destruction, the Prophet identified the slain figure as al-Uzza and said the Arabs would have no Uzza thereafter.
rows.anchor: ‘Uzzâ o idi, artık bundan sonra Arab’a Uzzâ yok’ buyurdu

rows.speaker: Mu‘cemü’l-büldan
rows.claim: Manat was a stone idol on the seashore at Qudayd, in the Mushallal district between Medina and Mecca.
rows.anchor: Menât, Medine ile Mekke arasında Müşellel nâhiyesinde Kudeyd nâm mevkide deniz sâhilinde dikilmiş taştan bir sanemin ismidir

rows.speaker: Mu‘cemü’l-büldan
rows.claim: Amr ibn Luhayy al-Khuza'i first erected Manat, bringing it from Syria and initially setting it around the Kaaba.
rows.anchor: ilk diken Amr b. Luhayy-ı Huzâî imiş, ibtidâ Şam tarafından getirmiş

rows.speaker: Mu‘cemü’l-büldan
rows.claim: Manat belonged to Hudhayl and Khuza'a and was revered with offerings by Quraysh and other Arabs; Aws and Khazraj did not count their pilgrimage complete until visiting it.
rows.anchor: Evs ve Hazrec onu ziyaret etmedikçe haclarını tamam saymazlarmış

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the eighth year after the Hijra, the Prophet sent Ali to destroy Manat; Ali brought back its possessions, including two swords, Mihzam and Resub, one of which is said to be Zulfiqar.
rows.anchor: Hazret-i Ali b. Ebî Tâlib’i gönderdi, o gitti onu hedmetti

rows.speaker: Taberî
rows.claim: Tabari derives al-Lat from Allah with a feminine ending, like masculine Amr/feminine Amra and Abbas/Abbasa; idolaters formed al-Lat from Allah and al-Uzza from al-Aziz.
rows.anchor: el-Lât, Allah lafzındandır. Tâ-i te’nîs ilhak edilmiştir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi derives al-Lat as the feminine of al-Lah: its original feminine form ended in ha, and after one of two h sounds dropped, the feminine t came to look like a root letter.
rows.anchor: el-Lât الل َّوَه’in te’nîsidir. Aslı ال َّلاهَةُ denilmekti

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Other derivations connect al-Lat to gathering or circling around it, or, in Yaqub's Ruways reading with doubled t, to latta, crushing or mixing.
rows.anchor: Etrafında toplanılmak ve dolaşılmak mânasıyla لَوَى aslı لَوْيَه olduğu da söylenmiştir

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: A report says a man mixed oil and sawiq and fed it to people, who grew plump; he was then worshipped, an idol made in his likeness, and named al-Lat.
rows.anchor: vaktiyle bir adam yağ ile sevık karıp halka yedirir ve yiyenler semirir idi

rows.speaker: Râzî
rows.claim: Razi says this derivation would make al-Lat masculine, but the author answers that interpreting it as an image preserves its feminine gender, as the verse's context requires.
rows.anchor: Râzî ‘buna göre Lât erkek olmuş oluyor’ demiş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Uzza is plainly the feminine of a'azz, like the feminine aziza.
rows.anchor: Uzzâ da belli ki ‘e‘azz’in müennesi olarak azîze demek gibidir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Manat may derive from mana, meaning decree, death, or hope, or from naw' as in Ibn Kathir's reading mana'a, perhaps alluding to sacrifices poured there or hopes for rain.
rows.anchor: mânasına “mena”dan, yahut İbn Kesir kıraatinde

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Manat 'the third, the other' mocks and disparages the idols: the first phrase sneers that the audience saw three after their companion saw two.
rows.anchor: ٱلثَّالِثَةَ ٱلْأُخْرَىٰٓ diye tavsif tehekküm ve tahkir içindir

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ukhrā commonly means 'the other,' but its original comparative sense from delay can also imply 'the most backward,' thereby disparaging all the idols.
rows.anchor: teahhurdan tafdil olmak itibariyle yerine göre en geri

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Manat third also demotes it, although it had been erected earlier and was one of the greatest idols.
rows.anchor: Menât, daha evvel dikilmiş en büyük putları iken Lât ve Uzzâ’dan sonra üçüncü mertebe putlar meyânına düşürülmüş

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The challenge asks whether the men take male names for themselves while assigning female names to their deity; Arabic nouns are masculine or feminine, and the idols all had feminine names.
rows.anchor: Erkek isimleri kendiniz alıp dişi isimleri mâbuda veriyorsunuz öyle mi

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idolaters claimed these idols, supposedly erected in God's name, represented divine powers and angels; they believed angels were God's daughters and hoped to gain intercession by worshipping their images.
rows.anchor: putlar ilâhî kuvvetlerin ve melâikenin suretleridir, melâike Allah’ın kızlarıdır

rows.speaker: Mu‘cemü’l-büldan; Yâkūt-ı Hamevî
rows.claim: Yaqut reports that Quraysh chanted during the circumambulation that al-Lat, al-Uzza, and Manat were exalted cranes whose intercession was hoped for, treating them as God's daughters and intercessors.
rows.anchor: Kureyş Kâbe’yi tavaf ederken: وَال َّلاتِ وَالْعُ َّزى وَمَنَاةَ الث َّالِثَةِ الأُْخْرَى
